s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic scrotal swelling with acute worsening and a palpable testicular mass
salient_findings: Firm, smooth testis without discrete nodules or tenderness
Hypoechoic lesion in the left testis with internal blood flow on ultrasound
key_facts: 20-year history of left testicular bloating and dull pain
Acute worsening of symptoms over the past 10 days
Left testis is enlarged, firm, and smooth
Transillumination of the left testis is negative
Scrotal Doppler ultrasound shows a hypoechoic lesion in the left testis
Internal blood flow is present in the hypoechoic lesion
Bilateral epididymal cysts are present
Serum CA19-9 level is elevated at 57.5 U/mL
Alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and other tumor markers are within normal limits

shortlist.label: Seminoma
shortlist.why_kept: Most common testicular cancer, matches palpable testicular mass and elevated tumor marker

shortlist.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Common testicular cancer, matches palpable testicular mass and elevated tumor marker

shortlist.label: Testicular lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches chronic scrotal swelling and acute worsening, with a palpable testicular mass

shortlist.label: Leydig cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Matches testicular mass and can cause hormonal imbalances, although less common

shortlist.label: Testicular teratoma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches palpable testicular mass and can cause elevated tumor markers, although less common

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of a long-standing, slowly enlarging testicular mass with recent acute worsening, along with the ultrasound findings of a well-circumscribed hypoechoic lesion and the laboratory finding of an elevated CA19-9 level, is most consistent with a Leydig cell tumor. Leydig cell tumors can produce various substances leading to hormonal imbalances and can have elevated tumor markers such as CA19-9.

rejected.label: Seminoma
rejected.why: Seminomas typically present with more rapid growth and often have elevated human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) levels, which is not the case here.

rejected.label: Non-seminomatous germ cell tumor
rejected.why: These tumors usually have a more complex appearance on ultrasound and often have elevated alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) levels, which is not seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Testicular lymphoma
rejected.why: Lymphomas of the testis are more common in older men and often present with more systemic symptoms and involvement of other lymph node groups, not described in this case.

rejected.label: Testicular teratoma
rejected.why: Teratomas can have a varied appearance on imaging but often contain elements from all three germ layers, and the description provided does not specifically suggest this type of tumor.
